newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL AND EAST EUROPE - DEC 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL AND EAST EUROPE - DEC 2.

text.p: AUSTRIA
DER STANDARD
- Animal-food maker Tagger's chief Helmut Sieber wants to expand the plant in Graz in southern Austria to make it the company's European head office.
- The Vienna bourse wants to introduce more stocks to continuous trade and plans a restructuring of blue-chip index ATX.
- Austrians remain pessimistic about the country's economy. However, public sentiment has improved since the beginning of summer, a study by research institute IMAS says.
- The far-right Freedom Party has presented plans to found its own workers union before Easter.
DIE PRESSE
- With the monopoly of rubbish collecting firm ARA abolished from December 1, new companies are planned in this sector.
- Creditanstalt sees big potential in eastern Slovakia as a centre for trade with Ukraine and Poland.
KURIER
- The number of civil servants taking early retirement is steadily declining as financial disadvantages and stricter controls are showing their effects.
SLOVAKIA

NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said he did not expect parliament to approve any significant changes to the proposed 1997 state budget, planned with a deficit of around 37 billion crowns.
- President Michal Kovac and Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik on Sunday left for an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) summit, starting today in Lisbon.

- Defence Minister Jan Sitek said Slovakia was interested in purchasing Russian KAMO-52 helicopters and JAK-30 aeroplanes. The equipment should be delivered in part repayment of Russian debts to Slovakia, Sitek said.

- Ivan Saktor, President of the Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ), said KOZ would not sign next year's general agreement with the government if parliament ignors all its proposed amendments to the 1997 state budget. Saktor said the proposed budget, if approved, could result in social conflict.
- The troubled heavy engineering company and major arms producer Povazske Strojarne a.s., claims it is owed some 1.3 billion crowns.

PRAVDA - The 1997 draft budget includes a paragraph according to which any claim against the Slovak Republic which had not been acknowledged by the government can not be registered as government debt to the central bank. This may finally end arguments with the Czech Republic over some 24 billion crowns in debts, claimed by the Czechs but never acknowledged by the Slovak side.
- Dozens of Slovak trucks were cought in the 12-day nation-wide truckers strike in France. Financial damages from the strike, promised by the French government, will be calculated next week.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, plans to sell property worth some 70 billion crowns next year. The NPF said it expected 1997 revenues of 15.8 billion crowns, of which 4.7 billion should come in cash and 11.1 billion crowns should be paid in privatisation bonds.
- Slovakia has signed a free-trade agreement with Lithuania effective January 1.
- Alcatel SEL TLH has signed a contract with the state telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie, worth some 1.08 billion crowns, for supplies of digital exchanges next year.
ROMANIA
LIBERTATEA
- The Oltchim SA chemical plant won a bourse quotation, bringing to 17 the number of listed stocks.
- Romania is expected to face petrol shortages until the end of the year due to lack of hard currency to import crude.
- The prices of milk and dairy products are expected to rise by up to 20 percent.
- Ex-president Ion Iliescu, now leader of the Party of Social Democracy, pledged to restructure the party and give it new lines of action before year's end.

- Controversial Syrian businessman Zaher Iskandarani says in interview he is the largest single individual investor in Romania. Iskandarani was recently released from jail pending a trial for alleged cigarette smuggling and tax dodging worth 41 billion lei.
- Romanians gathered by tens of thousands in Alba Iulia on Sunday to hear President Emil Constantinescu speak in the Transylvanian town.
- Constantinescu left for Lisbon on Sunday to attend the OSCE summit.
- Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea is expected to announce the new cabinet on Thursday.
CZECH REPUBLIC

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Wages increased by 18.4 percent to 9,214 crowns a month in the third quarter of 1996 as compared to the same period a year earlier when average gross wages amounted to 7,784 crowns a month.
- The Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) will support the proposed 1997 state budget on condition that reforms are pushed through on liberalisation of rents and energy prices, and cuts in taxation.
- Vladimir Stehlik, the general manager of the Poldi steelmill who has been in prison since last Wednesday with his son Marek, has sent his employees home for a one-month holiday.
- Value-added tax (VAT) should be decreased in the not too distant future, according to Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik. VAT will make up more than a fifth of state income next year.

- An analysis of Czech Railways' financial situation, which will be used as the basis for its restructuralisation, must include more information on tariffs, state grants and proposals for the development of train routes, said Transport Minster Martin Riman. The proposal should be ready by December 20.
- Aero Vodochody shareholders failed to approve a proposed debt removal plan during their general meeting on Friday, according to the chairman of the board of directors, Jaroslav Borak.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Motoinvest intends to leave the capital market by the end of March, 1997, according to Motoinvest's general manager Pavel Tykac. Tykac stated that the capital market is to risky.
- More and more Czechs are investing their money elsewhere than in traditional bank accounts, including construction savings banks, pension funds and insurance companies.
PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel voiced his support for Petr Pithart to lead the newly-formed Senate. Pithart was the chairman of the federal parliament in the two years following 1989.
- Pragobanka is currently raising its basic capital by 500 million crowns. The bank's basic capital is currently 1.86 billion crowns, according to Pragobanka spokesman, Dusan Michelfeit.
CROATIA
VJESNIK
- The Croatian railway company (HZ) management is calling on the staff to end their protest, but the railway workers continue the strike.

- Croatian customs services to be restored on four border crossings between Croatia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on Tuesday. The move is a result of an agreement signed between U.N. Transitional Administrator general Jacques Klein and the head of Croatian customs services Josip Knezic.
- Stock exchange: All prices went down last week and very little trading was reported on both Zagreb and Varazdin markets.
VECERNJI LIST

- The assistant foreign minister Hido Biscevic claims in an interview that the integration of Eastern Slavonia should be made an exclusively internal issue, which the Croatian authorities should reslove in cooperation with UN Transitional Administration in the region.
- Construction of the Zagreb-Gorican motorway continues despite harsh weather conditions.
SLOBODNA DALMACIJA

- Results of an independent telephone survey show some 68.3 of the 300 interviewed people from all over Croatia think that Croats are living poorly, while 48.7 of them believe the current authorities are unable to improve their social status.
